result_text:
Suppliers now carry payment terms in days, defaulting to 30. You can set them at registration and change them later. The full `mvn -o test` run passes.

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT DEFAULT 30 NOT NULL CHECK (>= 0)`.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: the record has a new `paymentTermsDays` component. I kept the old 5-argument constructor, which uses 30, so the existing call sites and tests compile unchanged. The new 6-argument constructor takes the terms.
- **`DataStore.java`**:
  - `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms, so renegotiating is an `updateSupplier` with a new value.
  - `listSuppliersByName`, `listSuppliersByCountry`, `listSuppliersByMinimumRating` and `findSupplierById` read it.
  - I also added the column to the other queries that build a `Supplier` (purchase suggestions, performance, spending, purchased quantity, single-supplier categories). Those embedded suppliers would otherwise have shown 30 whatever was agreed.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: a new test covers the default of 30, registering with 45 days, changing to 14, and seeing 14 in all four listings.

I didn't add a service-level check on the number of days. Only the database rejects negative values, with an `IllegalStateException`.
